questions.question:
Assertion (A): Gold and platinum jewellery do not tarnish or corrode even when worn daily in moist air.
Reason (R): Gold and platinum are placed at the bottom of the reactivity series and are noble, unreactive metals.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Gold and platinum are noble metals situated at the very bottom of the reactivity series. They do not react with atmospheric oxygen, moisture, or acid gases under normal conditions, preventing corrosion. Reason correctly explains Assertion.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Food packaging cans are electroplated with tin (Sn) rather than zinc (Zn).
Reason (R): Zinc is chemically more reactive than tin and could react with organic food acids to form toxic metal salts.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Zinc has a higher oxidation potential than tin and readily reacts with weak organic acids present in fruits and vegetables, causing food poisoning. Tin is less reactive and safely prevents contact between food and iron.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Photosynthesis in green plants is classified as an endothermic reaction.
Reason (R): Sunlight photon energy is continuously absorbed by chlorophyll pigments to synthesize glucose from CO₂ and H₂O.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + Sunlight (Energy) → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. Energy is absorbed from the environment to drive this biochemical synthesis, satisfying the definition of an endothermic reaction. Reason is correct explanation.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): When copper powder is strongly heated in a china dish, dense brown fumes are observed.
Reason (R): Copper powder oxidizes to form black copper(II) oxide (CuO).
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is completely FALSE because heating copper produces NO brown fumes (brown fumes are NO₂ from lead nitrate). Copper simply coats with a black layer of CuO (2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO). Reason (R) is TRUE.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The reaction Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu is a single displacement reaction.
Reason (R): Zinc is higher than copper in the reactivity series and displaces copper from its aqueous salt solution.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: In a single displacement reaction, a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound. Zinc displaces copper because Zn has higher reactivity than Cu. Reason correctly explains Assertion.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): White silver chloride crystals turn grey when exposed to sunlight.
Reason (R): Metallic copper displaces silver from silver chloride crystals.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is TRUE because AgCl decomposes into grey silver metal in sunlight: 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂. Reason (R) is completely FALSE because no copper is involved; it is a photolytic decomposition caused by sunlight photons.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): When the pH of rain water drops below 5.6, it is called acid rain.
Reason (R): When acid rain flows into rivers, it lowers the pH of the river water, making the survival of aquatic life difficult.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true facts from NCERT. Rain with pH below 5.6 is acid rain by definition. Acid rain flowing into rivers indeed jeopardizes fish and aquatic organisms. However, (R) describes the ecological impact, not the chemical definition of (A).
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Baking powder is used in making cakes instead of pure baking soda.
Reason (R): Baking powder contains tartaric acid, which neutralizes the bitter-tasting sodium carbonate produced during the thermal decomposition of sodium hydrogencarbonate.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Baking powder is a mixture of baking soda (NaHCO₃) and a mild edible acid like tartaric acid. On heating, NaHCO₃ yields basic Na₂CO₃ which tastes bitter; tartaric acid reacts to neutralize it into a pleasant-tasting sodium salt.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Plaster of Paris Storage
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Plaster of Paris must be stored in moisture-proof airtight containers.
Reason (R): On exposure to atmospheric moisture, Plaster of Paris absorbs water and sets into a hard solid mass of gypsum.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½H₂O → CaSO₄·2H₂O (Gypsum). Plaster of Paris reacts with moisture to form a hard solid mass of gypsum, rendering the powder useless if not kept in airtight containers.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Tooth decay begins when mouth pH falls below 5.5.
Reason (R): Tooth enamel made of calcium phosphate reacts with salivary amylase to form soluble calcium carbonate.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true: tooth decay begins below pH 5.5. Reason (R) is false because tooth enamel (calcium hydroxyapatite) is corroded by organic acids produced by bacteria degrading sugars, not by salivary amylase.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Copper(II) oxide reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form a blue-green solution of copper(II) chloride and water.
Reason (R): Metallic oxides are basic in nature because they react with acids to produce salt and water.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: CuO (black) + 2HCl → CuCl₂ (blue-green) + H₂O. Because copper oxide reacts with an acid to yield salt and water (neutralization), it confirms the basic nature of metallic oxides.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Aqueous solutions of glucose and alcohol do not conduct electricity through an immersion circuit.
Reason (R): Although glucose and alcohol contain hydrogen in their molecular formulas, they do not ionize in water to liberate free H⁺(aq) ions.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Conduction of electricity in liquids requires mobile charge carriers. Because glucose and alcohol form molecular solutions rather than ionic solutions, no free H⁺ ions are available to conduct electric current.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Ionic Compounds Melting Points
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Ionic compounds like sodium chloride (NaCl) and magnesium oxide (MgO) have very high melting and boiling points.
Reason (R): A considerable amount of energy is required to break the strong inter-ionic electrostatic attractions holding oppositely charged ions in the crystal lattice.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Ionic compounds are formed by electrostatic attraction between cations and anions. Because these electrostatic forces are very strong, a high amount of heat energy is needed to break the ionic bonds, resulting in high melting and boiling points.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Solid potassium chloride (KCl) does not conduct electricity through an electrical circuit.
Reason (R): In the solid state, ions are held rigidly in crystal lattice positions by strong forces and cannot move freely.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Electricity conduction in electrolytes requires mobile charged particles. In solid ionic compounds, ions are locked in fixed positions and unable to translate, preventing electrical conduction. In molten or dissolved state, ions become mobile.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Thermit reaction between iron(III) oxide and aluminium powder produces iron in the molten state.
Reason (R): The displacement reaction of Fe₂O₃ with aluminium is highly exothermic, liberating enough heat to exceed the melting point of iron.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) → 2Fe(l) + Al₂O₃(s) + Heat. The displacement reaction is so tremendously exothermic that iron is produced in liquid molten state (over 1538°C), enabling on-site welding of broken railway tracks.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sodium metal is extracted by the electrolysis of its molten chloride and not by carbon reduction of its oxide.
Reason (R): Sodium has a higher affinity for oxygen than carbon does, so carbon cannot reduce sodium oxide to sodium metal.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Highly reactive metals high up in the reactivity series (K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al) have very high chemical affinity for oxygen, stronger than carbon's affinity. Therefore, carbon cannot reduce their oxides. They must be extracted by electrolytic reduction.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A galvanized iron sheet does not rust even if its zinc coating is scratched and the underlying iron is exposed.
Reason (R): Zinc is more reactive than iron and oxidizes preferentially, providing sacrificial protection to the iron underneath.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Zinc has a higher oxidation potential than iron (Zn is higher in the reactivity series). When exposed to air and moisture, zinc corrodes preferentially, sacrificing itself to prevent iron from losing electrons and forming rust.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Electrical Conductivity of Alloys
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Pure copper is used for electrical transmission lines, whereas brass (Cu + Zn) and bronze (Cu + Sn) are not.
Reason (R): The electrical conductivity and melting point of an alloy are generally lower than those of its pure constituent metals.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Alloying disrupts the regular metallic crystal lattice, increasing electron scattering and lowering electrical conductivity. While pure copper is an excellent electrical conductor, brass and bronze have higher electrical resistance, making them unsuitable for power lines.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Unsaturated hydrocarbons like ethene and ethyne are much more reactive than saturated alkanes.
Reason (R): The presence of carbon-carbon double or triple bonds provides sites of high electron density that readily undergo addition reactions.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) are unreactive with most reagents and undergo only substitution. Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain weaker pi bonds in double/triple bonds that break easily to add other atoms (such as hydrogen, halogens), making them much more reactive.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Sunlight in Methane Chlorination
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The reaction of methane with chlorine does not occur in dark conditions but takes place rapidly in the presence of sunlight.
Reason (R): Ultraviolet light in sunlight provides photon energy to cleave chlorine molecules (Cl₂) into highly reactive chlorine free radicals.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: In the dark, methane and chlorine do not react because alkanes are stable. Sunlight (UV radiation) homolytically cleaves the Cl-Cl bond into chlorine free radicals, initiating the rapid substitution chain reaction: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Glacial Acetic Acid Freezing
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Pure ethanoic acid is commonly called glacial acetic acid.
Reason (R): Ethanoic acid has a melting point of 290 K (17°C) and freezes into an ice-like solid during cold winters in temperate regions.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: The melting point of pure ethanoic acid is 290 K (17°C), and hence it often freezes during winter in cold climates. Because it forms glacier-like icy crystals upon freezing, pure ethanoic acid is named glacial acetic acid.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In the preparation of ethyl ethanoate, a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid are added to the reaction mixture of ethanoic acid and ethanol.
Reason (R): Concentrated sulfuric acid acts as a catalyst and a dehydrating agent, absorbing the byproduct water to shift equilibrium forward.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Esterification is a reversible reaction: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Concentrated H₂SO₄ catalyzes the reaction and also absorbs water, preventing the backward hydrolysis of the ester and maximizing the yield of sweet-smelling ester.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Soaps in Hard Water
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Soaps are ineffective for washing clothes in hard water.
Reason (R): Calcium and magnesium ions present in hard water react with soap molecules to form an insoluble precipitate called scum.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Hard water contains dissolved Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ salts. Soap molecules react with these ions to form insoluble calcium and magnesium stearate/palmitate (scum), which precipitates out and wastes soap, preventing lather until all divalent ions are removed.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Synthetic detergents can be used effectively for washing even in hard water without forming scum.
Reason (R): The charged sulfonate (-SO₃⁻Na⁺) or ammonium heads of detergents do not form insoluble precipitates with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Detergents are sodium salts of sulfonic acids or ammonium salts with halides. The charged ends of these compounds do not form insoluble precipitates with the calcium and magnesium ions in hard water, allowing them to lather freely and cleanse efficiently.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Industrial ethanol is deliberately denatured by adding copper sulphate and pyridine.
Reason (R): Copper sulphate gives ethanol a blue color so that it can be easily identified and prevented from illicit beverage consumption.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: To prevent misuse of ethanol for drinking, it is made unfit for consumption by adding toxic methanol/pyridine and dyes like copper sulphate to impart a distinctive warning blue color.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Aerobic vs Anaerobic Energy
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Aerobic respiration in mitochondria generates much more energy than anaerobic respiration in yeast or muscle cells.
Reason (R): In aerobic respiration, glucose is completely oxidized into carbon dioxide and water, generating up to 38 ATP molecules per glucose molecule.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Complete breakdown of pyruvate in the presence of oxygen occurs in mitochondria, yielding CO₂, H₂O, and a large release of energy (approx. 38 ATP). In anaerobic respiration, incomplete breakdown yields only 2 ATP.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Ventricles have significantly thicker, more muscular walls than the atria in the human heart.
Reason (R): Ventricles have to pump blood out into various organs under high pressure, whereas atria only receive blood and push it into the ventricles.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Since ventricles have to pump blood into various organs (the right ventricle to the lungs, the left ventricle to the entire body), they have thicker muscular walls than the atria do.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Double Circulation in Mammals
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Birds and mammals possess a four-chambered heart with complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
Reason (R): Warm-blooded animals have high energy requirements to maintain a constant internal body temperature regardless of ambient environment.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Separation of right and left heart chambers ensures that oxygenated blood does not mix with deoxygenated blood, providing a highly efficient supply of oxygen needed for cellular thermoregulation in homeothermic birds and mammals.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Transpiration Utility in Plants
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Transpiration is considered a necessary process for tall terrestrial trees.
Reason (R): Transpiration helps in the absorption and upward movement of water and dissolved minerals from roots to leaves, and also helps in temperature regulation (cooling).
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Transpiration helps in the absorption and upward movement of water and minerals dissolved in it from roots to the leaves. It also helps in temperature regulation of the plant canopy on hot sunny days.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Active Translocation in Phloem
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Translocation of food in phloem is an active physiological process requiring ATP energy.
Reason (R): Sucrose is actively loaded into phloem sieve tubes using ATP, increasing osmotic pressure to drive water and nutrients towards low-pressure sink tissues.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Translocation in phloem is achieved by utilising energy. Material like sucrose is transferred into phloem tissue using energy from ATP, which increases osmotic pressure and moves materials according to plant needs.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Tubular Reabsorption in Kidneys
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Although the initial filtrate produced daily by kidneys is about 180 litres, the volume of urine excreted per day is only about 1 to 2 litres.
Reason (R): Over 99% of the initial glomerular filtrate is selectively reabsorbed along the tubular parts of nephrons into surrounding blood capillaries.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: The initial filtrate contains large volumes of water, glucose, and salts. Because the body cannot afford massive fluid loss, selective reabsorption recovers more than 99% of the filtrate back into the bloodstream.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Plant Excretion via Leaf Abscission
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Deciduous trees shed their leaves seasonally as a method of metabolic excretion.
Reason (R): Many toxic metabolic waste products in plants are safely sequestered in the vacuoles of older leaf cells that turn yellow and fall off.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Plants store many waste products in cellular vacuoles. Waste products may be stored in leaves that fall off, effectively discarding accumulated metabolic wastes without requiring specialized excretory organs.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Case Study - Muscle Cramps in Sprinting Athletes
questions.question: During a 100-metre race, an athlete suddenly experiences severe and painful calf muscle cramps. What biochemical reaction inside the muscle cells caused this condition?
options: Accumulation of excess urea in the muscle capillaries
Complete dehydration of skeletal bones
Breakdown of cellular ATP into toxic methanol
Anaerobic breakdown of pyruvate into lactic acid due to temporary oxygen deficiency
questions.explanation: When there is a lack of oxygen in human muscle cells, pyruvate is converted into lactic acid (a 3-carbon molecule). The sudden build-up of lactic acid in our muscles during vigorous physical activity causes painful cramps.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Case Study - Chronic Gastric Peptic Ulcers
questions.question: A patient suffering from stomach ulcers experiences intense burning epigastric pain. Biopsy reveals erosion of the stomach mucosal lining. Which secretion failed to protect the stomach wall?
options: Pepsin enzyme secreted by chief cells
Bile secreted by the liver
Mucus secreted by gastric mucous neck cells
Salivary amylase from the mouth
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, mucus protects the inner lining of the stomach from the corrosive action of hydrochloric acid. If mucus secretion is compromised (or broken down by Helicobacter pylori), acid burns the stomach wall, resulting in painful peptic ulcers.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A person suffering from damage to the cerebellum can think clearly and speak intelligently, but stumbles while trying to walk in a straight line.
Reason (R): The cerebrum governs conscious intelligence and speech, whereas the cerebellum coordinates motor equilibrium, balance, and precision of voluntary movements.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: The cerebrum is the seat of memory, speech, and intellect, which remain intact after isolated cerebellar damage. However, because the cerebellum coordinates voluntary muscle precision and balance, its injury impairs gait and motor stability.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Severe physical trauma to the medulla oblongata at the base of the skull causes instant death.
Reason (R): The medulla controls critical vital involuntary centers regulating continuous heartbeat, blood pressure, and respiratory rhythm.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: The medulla controls all fundamental involuntary autonomic life processes including cardiac contractions, respiratory rhythm, and vasomotor blood pressure. Damage to this area leads to immediate cardiac and respiratory arrest.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A houseplant kept beside an open window bends gracefully towards the incoming sunlight.
Reason (R): Auxin synthesised at the shoot tip is destroyed by light and ceases to exist anywhere in the plant stem.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true: shoots bend towards light (+ve phototropism). Reason (R) is completely false: auxin is NOT destroyed; rather, it diffuses away from the illuminated side to the shady side of the stem, stimulating cell elongation on the shaded side.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Mimosa vs Shoot Movement
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The drooping of leaves in Mimosa pudica is growth-independent, while the bending of a shoot toward light is growth-dependent.
Reason (R): Mimosa leaves move rapidly due to reversible changes in cell water turgor, whereas phototropic curvature occurs via directional cell elongation.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Movement in sensitive plants involves no growth; it occurs rapidly via turgor pressure changes in pulvini cells. In contrast, phototropism is a slow directional growth movement mediated by auxin-induced differential cell elongation.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Endocrine hormones circulate throughout the entire body in the blood, but act only on specific target organs.
Reason (R): Target organ cells possess specific molecular receptors on their surfaces that recognize and bind with matching hormones.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Although hormones travel universally in general circulation, only target cells with specific complementary receptor proteins can bind and respond to the hormonal signal.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Goitre and Himalayan Soil
questions.question:
Assertion (A): People living in high Himalayan mountain regions historically had a higher prevalence of simple goitre than coastal populations.
Reason (R): Mountain soil and water are deficient in iodine due to continuous glacial and rainwater leaching, whereas marine seafood and sea salt are rich in iodine.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Iodine is essential for thyroxin synthesis. High-altitude mountain soils have low iodine content, leading to dietary iodine deficiency and thyroid enlargement (goitre). Coastal populations obtain ample dietary iodine from seawater and seafood.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Pancreatic insulin secretion is controlled by a precise negative feedback mechanism.
Reason (R): Pancreatic beta cells sense rising blood glucose levels and secrete insulin; as glucose levels fall to normal, the stimulus for insulin secretion ceases.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Feedback mechanisms regulate hormone levels tightly. If blood sugar rises, pancreatic cells respond by producing more insulin. When the blood sugar level falls, insulin secretion is reduced, maintaining homeostatic equilibrium.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A man who has undergone a surgical vasectomy still produces semen during ejaculation and maintains normal secondary sexual characteristics.
Reason (R): Vasectomy cuts and ligates only the vas deferens; testes continue to produce testosterone directly into the bloodstream, and accessory glands still produce seminal fluid.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Vasectomy blocks only the transport of sperm cells through the vas deferens. The testosterone secreted by interstitial cells of testes enters blood directly, preserving masculinity. Seminal vesicles and prostate gland still contribute fluid, but the ejaculated semen lacks sperm cells.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): After a female undergoes tubectomy (surgical sterilization), regular monthly menstrual cycles continue normally.
Reason (R): Tubectomy blocks the fallopian tubes, preventing sperm from meeting the egg, but does not interfere with the hormonal cycle of the ovaries or the shedding of the uterine endometrium.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: In tubectomy, only the fallopian tubes are blocked. Ovaries continue to release eggs and secrete estrogen and progesterone into blood. The uterine lining continues to build up and shed monthly as menstrual flow because ovarian hormones are uninterrupted.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Assertion & Reasoning - Barrier Contraception vs STIs
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Condoms are considered superior to oral contraceptive pills for public sexual health.
Reason (R): Condoms act as a physical barrier that prevents transmission of sexually transmitted infections (like HIV and syphilis), whereas hormonal pills protect only against pregnancy.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Condoms prevent transmission of many infections during sexual act (such as bacterial gonorrhea/syphilis and viral HIV-AIDS/warts) in addition to preventing pregnancy. Hormonal pills alter ovulation but offer zero protection against pathogens.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Menstruation occurs once every approximately 28 days in women of reproductive age.
Reason (R): If an ovulated egg is not fertilized, the thick, vascular uterine lining (endometrium) prepared for implantation breaks down and is shed along with blood.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: The uterus prepares itself every month to receive and nurture the growing embryo. If fertilisation does not occur, this lining is no longer required and breaks down, shedding as menstrual discharge.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The placenta is a temporary endocrine and transport organ vital for embryonic survival.
Reason (R): The placenta contains chorionic villi surrounded by maternal blood spaces, providing a massive surface area for nutrient/gas diffusion and waste elimination without mixing maternal and fetal blood.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: The placenta contains villi on the embryo's side bathed in maternal blood spaces, providing high surface area for continuous exchange of glucose, oxygen, and metabolic wastes between two circulations separated by a thin placental membrane.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): All sugarcane plants grown in a field via stem cuttings are genetically almost identical to each other.
Reason (R): Vegetative propagation is an asexual mode of reproduction involving mitotic division of parental somatic cells without fusion of gametes.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Plants raised by vegetative propagation are genetically identical clones because all genetic material is derived from a single parent through mitotic cell division without meiotic recombination or fertilization.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Plant tissue culture is widely employed for producing virus-free ornamental and agricultural crops.
Reason (R): The apical meristem of a growing shoot tip is free from viral infections because cell division outpaces viral replication.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Using tissue culture, plants can be grown from a single plant in disease-free conditions. The shoot apical meristem is utilized because it divides faster than viruses can travel, providing pristine sterile tissue for micropropagation.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Self-pollination of heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt x Tt) yields an offspring population with approximately 75% tall plants and 25% dwarf plants.
Reason (R): The allele for tallness (T) is dominant and expresses in both homozygous (TT) and heterozygous (Tt) states, whereas dwarfness (t) is recessive and expresses only when homozygous (tt).
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: In a monohybrid cross Tt x Tt, the genotypic ratio is 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt. Because T is dominant, both TT (25%) and Tt (50%) exhibit the tall phenotype, giving 75% tall and 25% dwarf (3:1 phenotypic ratio).
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Muscular hypertrophy developed by an athlete through rigorous daily gym workouts is not inherited by their biological offspring.
Reason (R): Acquired somatic traits involve changes in non-reproductive bodily tissues and do not alter the nucleotide sequence of germ-line cellular DNA.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Acquired traits occur in somatic cells due to environmental interaction, diet, or exercise. Since somatic cells do not transmit genetic information to progeny, these traits cannot be passed on. Only changes in germ cell DNA (gametes) are heritable.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The phenotypic ratio and the genotypic ratio in the F2 generation of a classical Mendelian monohybrid cross are identical.
Reason (R): In the F2 generation of Mendel's monohybrid cross, the phenotypic ratio is 3:1 (Tall:Dwarf) whereas the genotypic ratio is 1:2:1 (1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt).
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is false because the phenotypic ratio (3:1) differs from the genotypic ratio (1:2:1) due to complete dominance of allele T over allele t. Reason (R) correctly specifies both ratios.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In many reptile species such as lizards and alligators, the biological sex of the offspring is not determined by genetic sex chromosomes.
Reason (R): The incubation temperature of the fertilized eggs during embryonic development directly governs sexual differentiation.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: NCERT explicitly states that in some animals, such as reptiles, sex determination is environmental rather than chromosomal: the temperature at which fertilized eggs are incubated determines whether the developing animal will be male or female.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Snails can change their biological sex during their lifespan.
Reason (R): Sex in snails is not permanently predetermined by genetic sex chromosomes.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: NCERT notes that snails can change sex, indicating that sex is not genetically fixed by sex chromosomes in these organisms, demonstrating non-genetic plasticity.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Refraction: Bending and Speed of Light
questions.question:
Assertion (A): When a beam of light travels obliquely from air into glass, the refracted beam bends towards the normal.
Reason (R): The speed of light inside glass is greater than the speed of light in air.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true: glass is optically denser than air, so light bends toward the normal. Reason (R) is false: the speed of light in glass (2.0 × 10^8 m/s) is slower than in air/vacuum (3.0 × 10^8 m/s). It is this deceleration that causes bending toward the normal.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.subtopic: Spherical Mirrors: Diversity of Image Types in Concave Mirrors
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A concave mirror can produce both real inverted images and virtual erect images.
Reason (R): The nature, size, and orientation of the image formed by a concave mirror depend entirely on the distance of the object from its pole.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and R explains A. When placed beyond focus F, the concave mirror forms a real and inverted image. When placed between pole P and focus F, it forms a virtual, erect, and magnified image.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.subtopic: Lens Power: Sign Convention for Concave Lenses
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The optical power of a concave lens is always designated with a positive value (+P).
Reason (R): A concave lens is a diverging lens with a virtual principal focus situated to the left of the optical center, giving it a negative focal length (-f).
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is false: optical power P = 1 / f. Since a concave lens has a negative focal length, its power is always negative (-P). Reason (R) correctly explains that concave lenses diverge light and have negative focal lengths.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The linear magnification produced by an ordinary flat plane mirror is exactly equal to +1.
Reason (R): A plane mirror forms an erect, virtual image whose height is identical to the height of the object and at an equal distance behind the reflecting plane.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Magnification m = h' / h. For a plane mirror, image height equals object height (h' = h), so |m| = 1. Since the image is virtual and erect, the sign is positive, giving m = +1. Reason (R) accurately explains this.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.subtopic: Refraction: Speed of Light in Diamond vs Water
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Light travels significantly faster in water than it does in diamond.
Reason (R): The absolute refractive index of diamond (2.42) is much greater than the absolute refractive index of water (1.33).
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Speed in a medium v = c / n. Because diamond has a much higher refractive index (2.42) than water (1.33), speed in diamond (≈ 1.24 × 10^8 m/s) is much less than speed in water (≈ 2.25 × 10^8 m/s). Hence light travels faster in water, and R correctly explains A.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A ray of light incident perpendicular to the surface of a rectangular glass block passes into the glass along a completely straight line without any deviation.
Reason (R): When angle of incidence is i = 0°, Snell's law (sin i / sin r = n) requires sin r = 0, meaning angle of refraction r = 0°.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: For normal incidence, the ray strikes parallel to the normal (i = 0°). From Snell's law, sin r = (sin 0°) / n = 0, so r = 0°. Thus, the ray does not bend at all.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.subtopic: Spherical Mirrors: Magnification Boundaries of Convex Mirror
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A convex mirror can produce a magnified virtual image when the object is held extremely close to its pole.
Reason (R): The focal length of a convex mirror is positive under the New Cartesian Sign Convention.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is false: a convex mirror NEVER produces a magnified image regardless of where the object is placed; it always forms a diminished virtual image (m < 1). Reason (R) is true: the focus of a convex mirror is behind the mirror, so f is positive.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.question:
Assertion (A): To an astronaut flying in outer space or walking on the Moon, the daytime sky appears pitch dark and black.
Reason (R): In outer space or on the Moon, there is no atmosphere with gas molecules or suspended particles to scatter sunlight toward the observer's eyes.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Scattering of light requires particulate or molecular scatterers. In the vacuum of outer space, sunlight travels in straight lines without scattering; unless looking directly at the Sun or illuminated celestial bodies, the sky appears completely black.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Stars twinkle prominently in the night sky, whereas planets shine steadily without twinkling.
Reason (R): Stars are extremely distant point sources of light whose rays suffer continuous deviations due to moving air layers, while planets are closer extended sources whose individual fluctuations cancel out on average.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). Planets act as extended discs composed of millions of point sources, so minor atmospheric disturbances across individual points average out to zero net variation in brightness.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Sun appears reddish-orange at dawn during sunrise and at dusk during sunset.
Reason (R): Rays from the horizon travel across a much greater thickness of Earth's atmosphere, causing shorter blue wavelengths to be scattered away while longer red wavelengths reach our eyes.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: At the horizon, sunlight travels through a larger atmospheric path length. Extensive Rayleigh scattering depletes the shorter blue/violet wavelengths from the direct beam, leaving predominantly the unscattered longer red wavelengths to reach our eyes.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.subtopic: Defects of Vision: Myopia Corrective Lens
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A person suffering from myopia requires spectacles fitted with convex lenses to correct their distant vision.
Reason (R): A concave lens is a diverging lens that diverges incoming parallel rays so they focus sharply on the retina instead of in front of it.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is false because myopia is corrected by a concave (diverging) lens, not a convex lens. Reason (R) is true: concave lenses diverge parallel rays so they converge precisely on the retina.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.subtopic: Defects of Vision: Presbyopia in Aging
questions.question:
Assertion (A): For most elderly human beings, the near point of distinct vision gradually recedes beyond 25 cm.
Reason (R): With advancing age, the ciliary muscles gradually weaken and the crystalline lens loses its elastic flexibility, reducing the eye's power of accommodation.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and Reason (R) explains Assertion (A). This age-related refractive decline is known as Presbyopia, which occurs as the ciliary muscles and crystalline lens lose their ability to increase converging power for close-up tasks.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.question:
Assertion (A): If one incandescent bulb in a series-connected chain of lamps burns out (fuses), all other lamps in the chain go off immediately.
Reason (R): In a series circuit, there is only one single continuous conducting path; an open fault at any point disconnects the entire circuit.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: In a series circuit, current must flow through every component sequentially. If a filament breaks, the circuit is open, current ceases completely (I = 0), and all lamps go dark.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Standard precision laboratory resistance coils are manufactured from alloys like Constantan or Manganin rather than pure elemental metals.
Reason (R): These alloys possess high electrical resistivity and an almost negligible temperature coefficient of resistance, ensuring resistance remains stable during heating.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Pure metals exhibit significant increases in resistance as temperature rises. Constantan and Manganin are chosen for standard resistors because their resistance is virtually temperature-independent over normal working temperatures.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Simply bending or curving a long copper wire into a zigzag shape without stretching it drastically alters its electrical resistance.
Reason (R): The electrical resistance of a uniform conductor is determined solely by its length, cross-sectional area, material composition, and temperature.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is false: bending a wire into curves or loops without stretching or compressing does not change its length, cross-sectional area, material, or temperature, so its DC resistance remains completely unchanged. Reason (R) correctly specifies the governing factors.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.question:
Assertion (A): An ammeter must always be connected in series with the circuit branch whose current is to be measured.
Reason (R): In a series connection, the exact same electric current flows through the measuring instrument as through the circuit load.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and Reason (R) explains Assertion (A). Current is identical at all points in a series loop, ensuring the ammeter accurately measures circuit current without altering branch flows.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.subtopic: Electrical Safety: Fuse Rating Upgrading Hazard
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Replacing a frequently blowing 5 A fuse with a 20 A fuse is a recommended solution to eliminate nuisance tripping in residential lighting circuits.
Reason (R): An oversized 20 A fuse fails to melt during wiring overcurrents, allowing house wires to overheat to incendiary temperatures and cause house fires.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is completely false and dangerous: upgrading a 5 A fuse to 20 A defeats the safety mechanism. Reason (R) is completely true: lighting wires rated for 5 A will melt their insulation and start fires before a 20 A fuse trips.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
questions.section: Section C: Natural Phenomena & Effects of Current

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Pure silver is the most electrically conductive metal known at room temperature.
Reason (R): Pure silver possesses the lowest electrical resistivity (approx. 1.60 * 10^-8 Omega m) among all metals.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and Reason explains Assertion. Electrical conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity (sigma = 1/rho). Because silver has the lowest resistivity of all metals, it is the best conductor of electricity.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The magnetic field inside a long current-carrying cylindrical solenoid is completely uniform.
Reason (R): Inside the solenoid, the magnetic field lines are represented by equidistant parallel straight lines running along the longitudinal axis.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). Equidistant parallel straight field lines indicate that the magnetic field has the exact same strength and direction at every point inside the interior of a long solenoid.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.subtopic: Force on Stationary Charges in Magnetic Field
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A stationary electric charge placed inside a powerful permanent magnetic field experiences a strong deflecting Lorentz force.
Reason (R): Magnetic force on a charged particle is governed by F = q * v * B * sin(theta), meaning magnetic fields exert zero force on charges at rest (v = 0).
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is false: a magnetic field exerts force ONLY on moving charges; stationary charges experience no magnetic force regardless of field intensity. Reason (R) is completely true: when v = 0, F = q * (0) * B = 0.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): An electric motor converts electrical energy into rotational mechanical energy.
Reason (R): A rectangular current-carrying coil placed in a magnetic field experiences equal and opposite forces on its two parallel arms, creating a couple that exerts continuous rotational torque.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). By Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, the upward force on one arm and the downward force on the opposite arm form a couple that rotates the armature shaft, converting electrical power into mechanical work.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The metallic chassis of high-power electrical appliances like washing machines and refrigerators must be connected to an earth ground wire.
Reason (R): Earthing provides an ultra-low resistance pathway for fault currents, ensuring user contact does not conduct dangerous currents through the human body.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and R explains A. If internal wiring insulation degrades and the live conductor contacts the metal body, current is shunted harmlessly to earth, instantly tripping the circuit breaker or blowing the fuse without shocking anyone touching the machine.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Copper rods are ideally chosen as the core material inside solenoids to manufacture powerful industrial electromagnets.
Reason (R): Soft iron has high magnetic permeability and loses its magnetism almost completely when the electric current is switched off, making it the ideal core material for temporary electromagnets.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is false: copper is diamagnetic and cannot be magnetized to form an electromagnet core. Reason (R) is true: soft iron is the correct ferromagnetic core material because it magnetizes intensely and demagnetizes promptly when current stops.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The concentration of non-biodegradable chemical toxins like DDT is found to be highest in top carnivores and humans.
Reason (R): Non-biodegradable chemicals cannot be broken down by cellular metabolism or excreted; they progressively bioaccumulate at each higher trophic level of a food chain.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and Reason explains Assertion. Because non-biodegradable chemicals cannot be metabolized, a predator that consumes many contaminated prey organisms absorbs and concentrates all their chemical toxins, resulting in maximum biomagnification at the top of the pyramid.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The flow of energy in an ecosystem is strictly unidirectional.
Reason (R): Solar energy captured by green plants cannot revert back to the Sun, and energy transferred to herbivores cannot flow backwards to autotrophs.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). Energy moves progressively through successive trophic levels in one direction only; unlike chemical nutrients, energy cannot be recycled back to lower levels.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The presence of the ozone layer in the stratosphere is essential for the survival of life on Earth.
Reason (R): Ozone molecules absorb damaging solar ultraviolet (UV) radiation, preventing high rates of skin cancer, cataract blindness, and genetic mutations in terrestrial organisms.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and Reason correctly explains Assertion. Stratospheric ozone acts as an optical filter absorbing harmful high-energy UV-B and UV-C rays that would otherwise induce severe cellular DNA damage in terrestrial life.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Decomposer microorganisms can be completely eliminated from a forest ecosystem without altering the health of green trees.
Reason (R): Decomposers such as saprophytic bacteria and fungi break down dead organic matter and plant litter, recycling essential mineral nutrients back into the soil for root absorption.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is completely false: without decomposers, dead plant matter would choke the forest and soil nutrients would be locked permanently in dead biomass, starving trees. Reason (R) is completely true: decomposers drive the biogeochemical recycling of essential minerals.
questions.citation: CBSE Class 10 Official 2023 Board Examination & NCERT Textbook
